title: The Cozy Potions of Sleepy World
summary: Seeker and his mouse friend Hattie spend a long day completely reorganizing and labeling Seeker's extensive potion closet, building custom shelves to accommodate rainbow and extra-small bottles. Once finished, they decide to try a mysterious, dark blue, swirly indigo potion covered in glowing stars. The potion instantly transports them to Sleepy World, a magical realm of ultimate coziness overseen by a fluffy, blue sleep dragon named Saluska. Saluska manifests custom, super-comfortable beds for each of them. To help Hattie fall asleep, Isabella tells a prehistoric bedtime story about Ancient Hattie the Mouse, prompting reflections on ocean-dwelling ancestors like Johnny the green mergirl and Violet Mergirl before everyone drifts off to sleep under a calm, starry sky.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: My father...

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Okay. Here we go.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: The story of Stars and Snories is starting. Snories.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Okey-doke.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: All right.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Now, the story part of Stars and Snories.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Ding dong, ding dong, Seeker. Ding dong, Seeker.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And Seeker said, 'Who is it?'

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: It's...

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Hattie Mouse.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: 'Come on in, Hattie Mouse,' said Seeker. 'Come on in, Hattie Mouse.'

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: I want to help you with your potion closet because Finny took your potions last... but it was last night.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: And he definitely asked you.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: But he only took one, two, three... He only took one potion: the fly potion you had to take you to Fly World because he wanted the fly potion so he could catch some flies.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And Seeker said, 'Yeah, Finn Cat asked very nicely if he could have a potion, and I wasn't sure what he was going to ask for because what kind of a world would Finn Cat want to go to? But turns out that Fly World sounded very interesting to him. I guess he likes to catch those. And you know, he hasn't even come back yet. He must still be there catching flies.'

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Yeah.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: He eats...

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: ...he eats five flies twice a day.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: 'That's a lot of flies,' said Seeker. 'I wouldn't want to eat any flies, would you, Hattie?'

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: No. I like cheese, seeds, nuts, berries.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh yeah, that sounds like a good, delicious diet.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Now...

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: I don't want to lose our appetite.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: You said you were coming over to help me with my potion closet?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Yeah, yeah.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Well, I suppose there are a few things you could help with. One is labeling the potion closet shelves. Another one is organizing the potions. Or, we could see if there's any strange, mysterious ones that we don't know where they go or what they do, and we could try one.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Um, I want to help you with all those things because I like doing all those things. I even like organizing.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh, wow. Well, all right.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: How about this? Let's take out all the potions and put them back in one by one.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Which order do they go in?

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Well, that's a good question, Seeker. Left, right, left, right, up, down, up, down?

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Well, they do go from left to right and top to bottom, but the question is, what order? Because we could sort them by size or by color.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Maybe by color. We can do a purple row, a red row...

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: ...so there's going to be an only red shelf...

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: ...and only yellow shelf...

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: ...and only green... and only red shelf, only orange shelf, and only yellow shelf...

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: ...and only green shelf, and only blue shelf...

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: All right.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: ...and then only purple shelf.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: This is going to be the most well-organized potion closet ever.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Those are the color shelves we're going to do.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And so, Seeker and Hattie started taking all the potions out of the closet. And once they'd done that, they made a red shelf, and an orange shelf, and a yellow shelf, and so forth. And before they knew it, they'd organized lots and lots of potions on different colored shelves. But then they realized there were some potions that couldn't go on any of those shelves. You know why?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Why?

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Because they had lots of colors. There was a potion that was both red and orange, and a potion that had red, blue, and yellow.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Oh, yeah. We can make some rainbow shelves. Rainbow shelves and some small potion shelves.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: You know, that's a good idea, too, because we have a lot of very small ones, and they could get lost among the other big potions. So, I think a small potion shelf is a really nice idea. And should that go down low by the floor or up high, do you think?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Um, down low.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Down low, okay. Okay.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Bang, bang, hammer, hammer, bang, bang.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh, you're making me a new shelf for the small potions, because it has to be a really small one, doesn't it? Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: I made it.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Thanks, Hattie.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: There we go. Now there's there's two shelves for the small potions. They have one, two on the light pink row, and one, two on the dark pink row.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Wow, okay, perfect, said Seeker.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And now...

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Bang, bang, hammer, hammer. I did the rainbow shelf.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh, thanks.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: I think that covers it. Did that include all of the potions, or are there... were there any left that they couldn't fit anywhere?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: There were more left.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: There was only one little problem.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Um, what?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: There was indigo and violet potions. So, here's, bang, bang, bang, I put together some indigo and violet shelves.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh, yes. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Here to put the indigo and violet potions on.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And by this time, now that they'd finished taking out, sorting, organizing, and putting back all the potions into the closet, including making a bunch of new shelves, Seeker and Hattie had worked hard all day and through the evening. And now they were very sleepy.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: But, but we need to do the other chores, said Hattie.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh, yeah. Um... well, there's the organizing, and the labeling.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: So, let's label each of the shelves. Label, label, label, label, label. So they wrote labels for each of the shelves.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And then, Seeker said, 'Hmm...'

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: 'You know, in this indigo area with all these dark blue, swirly potions, there's one that's dark blue and swirly, and has a beautiful speck of glowing stars. And I'm not sure where that potion would take us. Do you want to try it?'

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Yeah.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Okay, Hattie.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: I have an inkling, which is something that I wonder. I think this might be a Sleepy World potion.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And so, we can switch over to telling what happens with that potion as a Snory. You ready for that, Isabella?

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Is your nose okay?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: No. I mean, yes, yes, yes. Daddy, Daddy...

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: ...what about we do the rhyming sip part first?

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Yeah.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: ...on the words, and then we can do the sleepy potion part, the snory part.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Okay, that sounds great.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And Seeker said, 'Okay, Hattie, you can say the rhyme.'

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Zip-sip.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh, whoops, sip first. And they took a sip.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Kamoose-kajuice-kaboose, kamoose...

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: ...kajuice-kaboose, kamoose-kajuice-kaboose...

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: ...kamoose-kajuice-kaboose.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And there's a swirling and a tinkling sound.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: And now, we are...

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: ...now we take off the lantern.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Mm-hmm.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And I'll turn off my phone light.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: No, no, we need...

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And we'll turn on the owl stars, right?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Yeah.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Okay. We need the star. We need it to be dark.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: We need the stars. And we move on, like...

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Is that good?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: ...can we move up to like, up there, on that light?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: On the big circular one.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: I'll try.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Up on the big circular...

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: I'm trying, I'm trying.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh, almost.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: A little more, maybe?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Is that good?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: That's enough. Okay.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And shall we put on humidifier light, too, okay?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: No, not yet? Okay.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: No, that makes us not see the stars.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh, you're right. Okay.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And so, Seeker and Hattie appeared in the coziest world in the universe. It was Sleepy World.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: And who was there to greet them?

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Um, well, there was a very fluffy creature with big, droopy eyes because she was so sleepy. She was a huge, fluffy, blue sleep dragon.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: A blue sleep dragon.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And what was the sleep dragon's name, do you think?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Saluska.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Saluska.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: And Saluska, the sleep dragon, said... and she's one of our new characters.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Yeah, she's brand new.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Yeah.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And she said, 'Welcome, travelers, to Sleepy World. This is my world where everyone gets as cozy as can be.'

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: 'And you may choose whatever way you wish to become the most cozy. We have everything you might need.'

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: And, Dragon, Isabella has a very, very cozy place to sleep in her bedroom. Um, there's a little bit of toys, but pretty messy, but she has... but she does definitely have a bed in her room that has a big, fluffy cover...

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Wow.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: ...and some pillows, and a water bottle, a Yodo, which, if you're going to sleep in Isabella's bed, we should take out the Yodo.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Why is that?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Because, because, the stories might make everyone wide awake.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Because they like have some people imagining things, but they tell what they're imagining, so and they... and those stories kind of make me kind of sleepy, not all the way sleepy. So...

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: ...they're just not the kind of stories that you might know. Because that might distract you from sleeping in Isabella's bed.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh. Well, here in Sleepy World, you can set up your bed however you like. You can have a Yodo or no Yodo, and anything else you wish for.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: So, Seeker and Hattie...

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: And if you're very sleepy and you just want to go right to bed, then I can take out my Yodo.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh, thank you, Isabella, said Saluska, the sleep dragon.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And already, Saluska, the sleep dragon's big, fluffy, warm body and cozy, soft fur and deep voice were making Seeker and Hattie feel sleepy.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And they looked around, and they saw a beautiful, calm, starry sky, and it was dim, not very bright all around. And there were just mountains and piles of soft blankets and pillows everywhere.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And cozy beds to choose from, blankets of every shape, size, and color.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And Seeker said, 'I've always kind of wanted to have a big red bed. I like the color red. You know, I wear a red cloak usually.'

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Yeah.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And, and I'd also like to have red pajamas and a special, um, pajama cover for my beard so it doesn't scratch me while I'm sleeping, and maybe a little pajama hat for my head, and then I'll just curl up in that red bed.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: And, Seeker, there's some red fruits you can eat for breakfast tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh, thank you.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Um, they're called raspberries and strawberries.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh, that's wonderful. And you know what I'll do? I'll have red dreams of red fruits in my red bed while I sleep, said Seeker.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: And you can also have red watermelon, too.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Yum. And Saluska, the sleep dragon, made that beautiful, cozy red bed appear for Seeker, and he curled right up in it. And then, what did Hattie want for her bed?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: I want a pink bed with pink sheets with mice on them, and a pink blanket with purple stars, and, um, a cozy blue pillow.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And so, those things appeared, and Hattie climbed right in. But then she said, 'Wait, I need something to help me fall asleep in my cozy bed.'

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Hmm. Seeker and Saluska and Hattie thought about it a little bit, and they thought, maybe a very short story, or a lullaby?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: A very short story.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Okay. Do you want to tell Hattie's story? I don't know what her story is going to be about, do you?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: It was about Hattie's great-great-great-great-grandmother, who was also named Hattie, but she was Ancient Hattie the Mouse. And she lived a very busy life, dodging the dinosaurs, scurrying about in the prehistoric world that she lived in. And at the end of a very long day of adventures...

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: ...Grandma Hattie curled up in her burrow deep under the ground and pulled her covers of moss over her and laid her head on her pillow of leaves and went to sleep.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And Hattie the Mouse said, 'Wow, it's so nice to imagine my ancient ancestors. That makes me very sleepy.'

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Yeah, so...

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: And Isabella says, 'I do have some ancient ancestors that I really like, and I drew a picture of them.'

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh, you did?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Yes, of my ancient ancestors. I have some ancient ancestors.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Who are they?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Yeah. Their names are Muska and Johnny. Um, Johnny is one of my older daughters, and she is a mergirl, a green mergirl. She was ancient.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: And she had to find safe ways to be... she had to find some safe ways to hunt for food without getting chomped...

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: ...or bitten.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Wow.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: And also, there was also, um, and they had one ancient one named Hattie...

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: ...who also lived in the ocean and had to find safe ways to hunt food without getting bitten.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: And she was one of my older cousins, named, um, named...

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: ...and, uh, after you, Hattie, her name is...

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: ...Blue... her name was Violet Mergirl.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Wow.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And so, as they all curled up in their perfectly cozy beds and imagined the worlds of their ancestors, they gradually became very sleepy.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: But Isabella didn't get a bed yet.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: She didn't get that.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And Saluska, the sleep dragon, said, 'I thought you already have the coziest bed in the world, Isabella. Would you like a new one to imagine?'

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: What would your bed be like?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Um, my bed would have a cozy blanket like my other one, and a mouse with a Sesame Street sheet on it, a Sesame Street pillow, and a blue covered pillow with a water bottle, some stuffies, a Yodo, some arts, and rails, and a place for me to get out that has no...

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: I see.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: That sounds like a wonderfully cozy bed.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: And my mama card.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And Saluska, the sleep dragon, made a bed just like that appear for Isabella, and she curled up into it and closed her eyes and fell asleep. And that's the end of our Snory.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: So now we turn on the stars.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And now it's time to do the diaper. My light first, my light first, my light first.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Wait, what did you say? We got to change your diaper?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Diaper.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh. All right. I'll turn on the light.

characters.name: Seeker
characters.description: A brave dwarven explorer and mediator, he resides in a glowing castle hub—a multiversal dock for skyships anchored within the skyline of New York City. From this urban sanctum, he conducts silver slime experiments and tends to wandering cats amidst a massive library. Frequently swapping between a red coat and a mystical purple cloak, his braided red beard remains his most eccentric tool, capable of catching small fish. A master of fusion, he combines ancient stone-craft with high-velocity mechanics, utilizing a legendary magic ladder to scale the shifting architecture of the realms. Whether brewing portal potions, harvesting floof-berries in Limbo with gemstone goggles, or aiding Buddy the Mouse, this walnut-loving student of the stars remains the hero who orchestrated the daring rescue of the world.

characters.name: Hattie the Mouse
characters.description: A nimble, friendly mouse of Possible Street and loyal friend to Izzy and Seeker, this brave artisan is the wife of Dimitar and mistress of the Workshop of Hats—a weathered hollow tree sanctuary on Cornell Street scented with cedar, ink, and peanut butter toast. Clad in her signature red cloak and pointy hat, she is a resourceful hatmaker whose spirit was forged against massive diggers and the rain-slicked Floofer Cloud. Within her paint-stained home, she carefully curates her husband’s library alongside her own hand-painted volumes while confronting a baffling supply mystery; the discovery of curious clover stickers signals a gathering shadow of intrigue she is determined to unravel.

characters.name: Finn Cat
characters.description: A character featured in a coloring picture with Worry-Worry Whale.

characters.name: Saluska
characters.description: A fluffy, big blue sleep dragon with droopy eyes who welcomes visitors to Sleepy World.

characters.name: Ancient Hattie the Mouse
characters.description: Hattie's prehistoric grandmother mouse who lived in burrow tunnels and dodged dinosaurs.

characters.name: Johnny
characters.description: Isabella's ancient ancestor who was a green mergirl living in the ocean.

characters.name: Violet Mergirl
characters.description: An ancient violet-colored mergirl cousin of Isabella's who also hunted for food in the deep seas.

characters.name: Isabella
characters.description: A towering Dimatar scholar and alchemist of Atsukeeseet, Mama Izzy is a clever kiddo at heart and a steadfast guardian of rooftop gardens and intricate dollhouses. Gifted with the power of flight, she navigates the open heights with aquatic grace, her massive frame often shielded by a special protective metal that glimmers even as she descends into the shadows. As a resourceful quartermaster, she employs red flashlights, gold-laced slimes, and pipe cleaners to mend a Lanternshark’s failing light, yet her generosity remains her hallmark; she freely shares her vast library, brokers homes for dragons, and teaches others to find the resonance in their own voices. Her most profound magic resides in her vast, soft blanket—a sanctuary of ultimate coziness—where she remains a brave, quick-witted protector to all who honor her singular request for absolute silence.

places.name: Fly World
places.description: A insect-filled world where Finn Cat goes to hunt and catch flies.

places.name: Sleepy World
places.description: The coziest world in the universe, characterized by calm starry skies, mountains of soft blankets, pillows, and a sleep dragon named Saluska.

places.name: The Ocean
places.description: The vast underwater home of Willa and Pout-Pout.
